summary: James Miller worked in sinology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge (~1994–1997) and Boston University (~1995–2000) before becoming Professor of Chinese Studies and Religious Studies at Queen's University Belfast.
James Montgomery studied at the University of Glasgow (~1980–1984). He held a post at the Faculty of Asian and Middle Eastern Studies, Cambridge in 1997 and taught Mario Kozah.
James Morison was an indologist who studied under Georg Bühler as a Specialschüler. He held a post as Librarian at the University of Oxford.

James Prinsep worked in indology, archaeology, and linguistics. He served at the India Government Mint in Kolkata (1819), the Benares Mint (~1820–1833), and the Asiatic Society (1832–1838), succeeding Horace Hayman Wilson in 1833.

Indologist and philosopher James R. Ballantyne studied at the University of Edinburgh under James Michael and Francis Johnson. He taught at the Scottish Naval and Military Academy, served as Principal at Benares Sanskrit College (1845–1861), and was India Office Library librarian.
Historian James R. Rush studied at Yale University from ~1971 to 1977. He took up a post at Arizona State University around 1990 and taught Brooke Schedneck.
James Rennell worked in history, archaeology, and indology. He held posts with the East India Company from 1762 to 1777 and with the Bengal Engineers in 1764.

Specializing in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, James Robson served as Assistant Professor at the University of Michigan (~2004–2008). In ~2008, he became Associate Professor of East Asian Languages and Civilisations at Harvard University.

James Sutherland Cotton, an indologist and historian, studied at Magdalen College School, Brighton College, Winchester College (~1860–1863), and Trinity College, Oxford (~1863–1867). He held a post at Queens' College, Cambridge from 1871 to 1874.

James Tod worked in history, archaeology, and indology. He held a post with the East India Company (~1798–1823) and later served as Librarian at the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (~1823–1835).
James W. Benson worked in indology and linguistics. He was Assistant Professor in Sanskrit at Harvard University (~1985–1991) and held a post at Wolfson College, Oxford starting in ~1991.

James W. Heisig studied at the University of Cambridge (~1971–1974), working in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He held posts at Nanzan University (~1978), the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture (1978–2001), and Pompeu Fabra University.
James Whitehill worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He was Professor of Religion at Stephens College (~1973–2004) and founded the Columbia Zen Center.

Linguist James Wilson Bright studied at Lafayette College (~1873–1877) and Johns Hopkins University (~1879–1882). He held posts at Cornell University (~1885) and Johns Hopkins University (~1885–1924).

Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thayé was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Thekchok Dorje and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (~1840–1892), and taught Karma Tashi Chophel and Khakyab Dorje.

Jamie Hubbard studied at UW–Madison (~1978–1986 under Minoru Kiyota) and Komazawa University (~1982–1984 under Kazuo Okabe). He served as Yehan Numata Professor and Conway Professor at Smith College (~1985–2021) in Buddhist and religious studies.

Jampa Losang Panglung worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1960 and studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1973–1979).

Jampa Mackenzie Stewart is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche and Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge, as well as teacher Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

Jampa Tegchok studied at Sera Monastery until ~1959. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1971–1978), Nalanda Monastery as abbot and teacher (~1982–1992), and Land of Medicine Buddha (~1998–2001).
Jan Chozen Bays works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Taizan Maezumi (~1977–1995) and Shodo Harada (~1995), becoming abbess at Great Vow Zen Monastery in ~2002.
